info.title: CivicOS platform API
info.description: Every HTTP endpoint of this installation, generated from its route files (scripts/build-openapi.mjs). Request and response bodies are JSON, typed from the TypeScript types the routes use where they declare them; errors are `{ "error": string }`. Sign-in rules follow the platform middleware and lib/auth/roles.ts: public sites and public reads are open, everything else needs an official's session or the machine credential named in each operation's security. `x-permission-rule` names the rule a change falls under (administrator, installation: a government-wide administrator of this nation, ministry, official, bearer, self-authenticated, public-write).

post.description: POST /api/access-log/retention { id } — the oversight side's confirmation of a rule that deletes from the access log (lib/data/retention.ts confirmByOversight()), after two administrators proposed and confirmed it: the data-protection authority's officials who can sign, or an auditor while none is named (canConfirmAccessLogRetention()); never an administrator.

get.description: /api/access-log — who read which restricted or secret record, searched, exported or was refused (lib/records/access-log.ts). Read by auditors and the data-protection authority's officials (canReadAccessLog()); nobody changes it through the API. With the chain's check and, for the data-protection authority, the unusual patterns of the last day. Reading the log is itself written to it (directions 15.5: oversight access is logged), as a search of register access-log.

post.description: /api/admin/officers/bulk — server-side bulk officer onboarding. Accepts a CSV or JSON array of {email,name,charter_id,role,title?} and forwards to civicos_admin_bulk_create_officers via the service-role client. Returns the substrate's per-row result so the UI can show which entries succeeded and which failed. Auth: callers must hold a platform-tier session OR pass the CIVICOS_PROVISIONING_SECRET as a bearer (so CLI/automation can use it without a UI sign-in). The substrate enforces the platform-tier check separately, so this route is a defense-in-depth gate, not the sole authorisation. Every batch that reaches the substrate is written to the platform audit chain (baseline audit §3.3): who called (the platform officer, or the provisioning secret named as such, since it names no person) and the counts received, created and failed — never an email, name or other row content. The shared secret is to be replaced by named officials (integration register 1.46).

The AI advisory for a console panel (per-nation opt-in; register 2.1). The body is validated (lib/ai/advisory-input.ts: types, ranges, a label cap, control characters stripped), each figure carries its SignalKind and the prompt tells the model which figures are samples. Every call is audited: who asked, the model, SHA-256 of the prompt and of the answer, and whether the model or the rule-based fallback answered. The request is operational data leaving the platform, so it goes through the data-sovereignty gate (lib/data/sovereignty.ts, category 'ai-advisory': off unless a named official enabled it); when it is off the panel gets the rule-based advisory and nothing is sent. The model service is the nation's choice (SovereignProfile.aiAssistantModel: the default provider or its own sovereign / on-premises model; lib/ai/model.ts). Each official may ask CIVICOS_AI_RPM times a minute (default 10).

source.description: Who answered: the model, or the rule-based fallback. Only 'model' may be shown as "AI advisory".

get.description: /api/audit/proof — single-entry verifiable inclusion proof. Given (scope, seq) the endpoint returns: - The audit chain prefix from genesis to seq, so a verifier can re-walk every prev_hash → hash relationship locally. - The targeted entry (== the last row in the prefix). - Every witness attestation that observed (scope, seq), so the verifier can confirm the recorded hash matches what witnesses saw at that time. - A server timestamp framing the proof. The output is the same shape the /api/substrate/export endpoint produces, so it loads directly into /gov/audit-replay (or any third-party copy of lib/audit/replay.ts). Auth: public read. Audit entries are already publicly readable per the RLS policy on civicos.audit_entries.

get.description: The platform audit chain, newest first, one page at a time (go-live review M-8): ?limit= (default 200, at most 1000) and ?before=<seq> for the page after; `total` is the chain's length and `nextBefore` the cursor for the next page (absent on the last one). Read by auditors and the data-protection authority's officials (canReadAuditChain() in lib/auth/roles.ts; step I0.1): the chain names who acted in every institution, independent ones included, and carries no institution to filter by. Each read is written to the access log as a search of register `audit` (repeats of the same page within a minute once), and a refusal as `refused`. The chain's integrity check stays public (/api/audit/verify).

The platform audit chain's verification, open to everyone (a transparency feature; the cover page shows it). Answered from the cached, incremental check (lib/data/store/audit.ts auditVerification, go-live review M-8): only entries appended since the last answer are hashed here; the whole chain is checked again off the request path. Limited per address (`publicRead`). A signed-in official may ask for the full check now with ?full=1; it runs in chunks that yield to other requests.

/api/audit/witnesses/keys — the public keys whose signed attestations of the audit chain the platform records (go-live review H-1). GET every registered key (public keys are public) POST { label, jwk, by } register a witness's public key (administrators: lib/auth/roles.ts ADMIN_ONLY) DELETE ?id=…&by=… revoke it; its earlier attestations stay, it attests no more The name recorded is the signed-in official's (withOfficial), never a typed one when someone is signed in. Each change is written to the substrate's audit chain (scope substrate:witnesses).

post.description: /api/audit/witnesses — record a witness attestation of the audit chain (go-live review H-1). A witness (an auditor, civil society, a peer institution) states "I saw scope S at seq N with hash H" and signs `S|N|H|label` with its own key. The credential is that signature: the key must be registered for the label by an administrator (/api/audit/witnesses/keys) and unrevoked, and the signature must verify, before the platform records the statement through the service role. Nobody else can write attestations (the substrate RPC is service-role only), and a statement is never replaced. POST { scope, observedSeq, observedHash, label, jwk, signature } 201 { witness } recorded 400 malformed 403 no registered key for the label matches, or the signature does not verify 409 this witness already attested that point 503 substrate not configured

POST /api/auth/account-changes/{id} { op: 'confirm' | 'withdraw', reason? } (lib/auth/account-changes.ts; plan phase 2, audit D). Confirm: an official who can sign at the independent institution the change waits for (or its administrator), a different person from the administrator who proposed it (canConfirmAccountChange()); when every institution has confirmed, the change is made and a reset code for a new account (or one asked for) is returned once, to this official, to hand over in person. Withdraw: the proposer or an administrator. Who acted comes from the sign-in; audited.

get.description: /api/auth/account-changes — account changes waiting for an independent institution to confirm (lib/auth/account-changes.ts; plan phase 2, audit D). GET: administrators see every change; any other signed-in official sees the changes waiting for their own institution and those they proposed. Confirming or withdrawing one: POST /api/auth/account-changes/{id}.

The signed-in official's own sign-in activity, newest first (lib/auth/activity.ts): sign-ins with a coarse device, failed attempts against the account, password and second-step changes, administrators' changes to the account.

GET /api/auth/citizen/callback — the identity service sends the citizen back here (lib/auth/citizen-oidc.ts); on success the citizen's session (lib/auth/citizen-session.ts) is set and they continue to the wallet.
GET /api/auth/citizen/start?from=/wallet/... — send the citizen to the nation's identity service (lib/auth/citizen-oidc.ts), with this browser's one-time state in a short cookie.

The signed-in official (register 15.4). GET: who is signed in, how officials sign in on this installation, and whether actions require it. POST signs in — with a platform account (email + password) or, when the substrate is connected, with the substrate's access token, checked by the server and matched to the officer register — or with a passkey ({ method: 'passkey', challengeId, response }, options from /api/auth/passkeys/options). A password sign-in whose account has a passkey is answered with passkey options for the second step, then sent again with { passkey: { challengeId, response } }. Officials who sign in through the government's identity provider start at /api/auth/oidc/start. DELETE signs out, ends the session on the server (review M-1), and answers with the provider's sign-out address when the session came from it. Every sign-in and sign-out is written to the audit chain; addresses never are. When the middleware asks GET about a change (x-civicos-change-path and -method) that the rules refuse, the refusal is written to the access log here (reference and rule only; lib/records/refusal-log.ts).

post.description: Change a platform account (administrators only; audited): disable or re-enable it ({ disabled }), or set its role and institution ({ role, institution }; institution null or "" for the whole government), or reset its second sign-in step when the official's phone is lost ({ resetTwoStep: true }; they set it up again at their next sign-in), or issue a one-time password reset code to hand over in person ({ issueReset: true }; shown once, expires in 24 hours). An account of an independent institution (now, or after the change) is changed by that institution's own administrator; an administrator serving the whole government proposes the change and it waits (202) for an official who can sign there (lib/auth/account-changes.ts, accountChangeRule()); administrators of another institution may not.

get.description: The government's identity provider for officials (OpenID Connect, lib/auth/oidc.ts). Administrators only (ADMIN_ONLY in lib/auth/roles.ts), every change audited; the client secret is sealed and never returned. GET: the configuration, the redirect URI to register at the provider, and the identities waiting for an administrator. POST { action }: 'save' { name, issuer, clientId, clientSecret?, tokenAuth?, scopes?, matchClaim?, groups?: { claim, rules: [{ group, role, institution? }] } | null, mfa?: { accept, amr?, acr? }, internalNetwork?, extraHosts?, enabled? } → reads the provider's discovery document and saves; 'enable' / 'disable'; 'decide' { requestId, decision: link | create | refuse, accountId?, account?, reason? } → link the identity to an account, make an account with a role, or refuse; 'unlink' { accountId } → remove an account's identity link. Independent institutions keep their own user administration (plan phase 2): making or linking an account of one, mapping a provider group to one, or unlinking one of its accounts is for its own administrators; an administrator serving the whole government uses Official accounts instead, where the institution confirms (lib/auth/account-changes.ts).

get.description: Platform accounts for officials (lib/auth/officials.ts). GET lists them (never password hashes): in full for an administrator (each such read written to the access log as one search with the count), as a directory (name, office, institution) for any other signed-in official. An administrator also gets the installation's two-step policy (`twoStep`: who must use the second sign-in step, who last set it), so the Official accounts screen shows it to substrate administrators too. POST creates one: the first account at installation, with the one-time setup code (`setupToken`, lib/auth/setup-token.ts: CIVICOS_SETUP_TOKEN or the code the server wrote to its output at start), every later one by an administrator. While the substrate is the sign-in method no platform account is created (409). An account of an independent institution (the legislature, a court, the head of state's office, an independent body) is created by that institution's own administrator; an administrator serving the whole government proposes it, and it waits (202) for an official who can sign there to confirm (lib/auth/account-changes.ts, accountChangeRule()). Administrators of another institution may not.

get.description: Where the government's identity provider sends officials back (the redirect URI registered there). GET ?code&state: the state must be the one this browser started with (its cookie) and is used once; the code is exchanged with the PKCE verifier, the ID token checked (signature against the provider's keys, issuer, audience, expiry, nonce) and the identity matched to an official account (lib/auth/oidc.ts). Then the signed session is set exactly as for any other sign-in. Open without a session; nothing happens without a valid state. Unlinked identities wait for an administrator (/admin/officials).

Sign in through the government's identity provider (OpenID Connect, lib/auth/oidc.ts). GET ?from=/path starts a sign-in: a fresh state, nonce and PKCE verifier are kept on the server for ten minutes, the state also in an httpOnly cookie for this browser, and the browser is sent to the provider. Open without a session (it is how officials get one).

post.description: Signing in with a passkey alone: POST gives the browser a fresh challenge (five minutes, used once) to sign with any passkey it holds for this platform; the answer goes to POST /api/auth/official { method: 'passkey' }. Open without a session (it is how officials get one), rate limited like every change.

get.description: The signed-in official's passkeys and security keys (WebAuthn; lib/auth/officials.ts, verification in lib/auth/webauthn.ts). GET lists them (name, when added and last used; never a key). POST { action }: 'options' → creation options for the browser (an account that already has a second step needs a session that passed it); 'register' { challengeId, response, name } → verifies the authenticator's answer and keeps its public key; 'remove' { id } → removes one (not the last second step the installation requires). Platform accounts only. Every change is audited.

Passwords of platform accounts (lib/auth/officials.ts). POST { action: 'change', current, next }: the signed-in official changes their own; every other session of theirs ends and this one is renewed. POST { action: 'reset', email, code, next }: no session; sets a new password with the one-time code an administrator issued (wrong codes count toward the sign-in lockout). The official then signs in as usual. Both audited; passwords and codes never appear in the audit chain.

get.description: The signed-in official's second sign-in step (authenticator app, RFC 6238; lib/auth/officials.ts). GET: whether it is on, whether the installation requires it, and the policy. POST { action }: 'start' → a new key (shown once) and its otpauth:// link; 'confirm' { code } → turns it on, returns ten recovery codes (shown once) and renews the session as having passed the second step; 'off' { code } → turns it off (not when the policy requires it); 'policy' { policy: none | signers | all } → administrators only. Every change is audited. Platform accounts only: substrate officers use the substrate's own sign-in.

get.description: The boundaries in force for the installed nation (both levels, with shapes), for maps to draw. Published boundaries are public information. ?at=YYYY-MM-DD for another date; &knownBy= for only what had been published by then.

The nation's own boundaries (lib/data/boundaries.ts): GET lists every version (without shapes); POST checks a boundary file (?dryRun=1 records nothing) and records it as a proposal for a different official to publish. The file goes either as JSON (`text` with `format` geojson | topojson, or `base64` for any format) or as multipart/form-data: `file` (GeoJSON, TopoJSON, a zipped Shapefile .zip or a GeoPackage .gpkg) and `body`, a JSON string with the other fields (level, source, validFrom, codeField, nameField, confirmFewer, note). The format is detected from the file (geojson | topojson | shapefile-zip | geopackage) unless `format` names it.

n.description: Version number for the nation and level, from 1.

validFrom.description: When the boundaries took legal effect (YYYY-MM-DD).

fileSha256.description: SHA-256 of the uploaded file as received.

reprojectedFrom.description: The coordinate system the file was reprojected from.

confirmFewer.description: The proposer confirmed that fewer units than before is intended (a merger of units).

get.description: /api/case-packages — the nation's procedures (lib/casework/packages.ts, design §6.3). GET: every version with its state. POST { op: 'draft', package } writes a draft (officials of the responsible institution); { op: 'approve', key, version, activeFrom? } approves it (an official who can sign there, different from its author, once its tests pass); { op: 'install-references' } drafts the reference procedures CivicOS ships that the installation does not have yet (administrators; drafts only); { op: 'load-demonstration' } loads the demonstration set (a sample act and the civil procedures approved under it; administrators, demo and training installations only, lib/casework/demo.ts); { op: 'draft-referral', institution } drafts that institution's referral procedure from the template (its own officials or administrators; lib/casework/referral.ts); { op: 'edit', key, version, changes } changes a draft in place (its form, evidence, day counts, citations: officials of the responsible institution; whoever changes it cannot approve it; lib/casework/packages.ts editDraft()). Publication (lib/forms/publication.ts): GET ?publication=<key>&version= gives the version's gates, the automatic checks and the human approvals apart, the register status they give and the acts recorded; POST { op: 'approval', key, version, approval: { kind, outcome?, note?, citation?, rollbackPlan?, releaseNotes?, environment? } } records one approval as an act of the signed-in official (never a status sent in the request). The form contract (lib/forms): GET ?form=<key>[&version=][&locale=] gives a procedure's form as it renders; ?contract=1 what a form may use (types, classes, named rules, patterns, approved lists, building blocks, exchange services); ?library=1 the form library (the specification's sixteen forms, the field series' contracts and the catalogue contracts CivicOS wrote in batches, each with what the loader reported, every deviation and its register status from the publication gates; ?form= and ?publication= answer for a library form too, a contract draft no procedure carries yet, whose approvals are recorded only on the procedure that carries it). A document's citation may be sent as { instrument, eId }: it is cited from the laws register here.

owner.description: The authority (resolved through the deployment profile) or an institution id.

authority.description: The permit type whose approved authority mapping governs this procedure's decisions, for a procedure the platform does not already classify (lib/permits/decisions.ts). Approved with the procedure by two officials.

appeal.description: The appeal: its days as the nation's law sets them (unset in a reference procedure; sampleDays only for demonstrations).

sampleDeadlines.description: Its day counts were filled from the reference's sample values in a demo or training installation (shown marked Sample; never approved in production).

editors.description: Officials who changed this draft after it was written (its form, day counts, evidence); none of them may approve it.

reference.description: Shipped with CivicOS as a reference; arrives as a draft the nation must approve.

Audit-chain anchoring cron — periodically broadcasts the head of every visible audit scope as a federation event of type 'audit.anchor' on channel 'constitutional'. External systems that subscribe to the federation stream get a continuous live record of where each chain pointed at known wall-clock times. Complements the witness-attestation system: - audit_witnesses table is the append-only, public, tamper-proof record (provable retroactively). - federation 'audit.anchor' events are the realtime broadcast channel (subscribers see it as it happens; consumers can persist externally for an independent record). The platform's own chain (lib/data/store.ts) is anchored too: its head is signed (lib/audit/sign.ts), written to the append-only anchor file outside the state (file mode, lib/audit/anchor.ts) and, with the substrate connected, broadcast as scope 'platform' with its signature. Without the substrate only the platform head is anchored. With CIVICOS_TSA_URL the head is first time-stamped by the nation's RFC 3161 TSA (lib/audit/tsa.ts) and the token travels with it. Auth: CIVICOS_CRON_SECRET as Authorization: Bearer (header only). Cadence: every 5–15 minutes. Idempotent — anchoring the same head produces an event with the same content, but federation events are append-only so duplicate broadcasts are allowed (consumers dedupe by (scope, seq) if they care).

get.description: Outbound federation webhook delivery worker. For each active civicos.event_webhooks row, finds federation events on its channel newer than its cursor and POSTs each to the registered URL with an HMAC-SHA256 signature header. On an all-2xx run the cursor advances to the last delivered event's at_ms; on the first failure the cursor holds (so the next run retries from the same point) and the failure is recorded. Every POST goes through the platform's safe fetch (go-live review M-5): public addresses only unless the nation allows its own network (CIVICOS_WEBHOOKS_PRIVATE=1), redirects never followed. get.description: Update watchdog cron — every minute (supabase/cron/schedule.sql). Concludes due probations for every nation: passes a release whose window ended healthy, records overdue health reports as missing, and on a confirmed failure either switches the software back to the last known good release or leaves it waiting for the nation's decision (ask-first, or a release that is not backward compatible). It never installs anything: it can only conclude probations and switch back to the last known good release. The same evaluation also runs when the chamber, a release, the publisher console or the health endpoint is read, as a fallback if the schedule stops. Auth: CIVICOS_CRON_SECRET as `Authorization: Bearer …` (header only), like every /api/cron/* worker.

get.description: Tamper-detection watchdog. Runs after witness-sweep on the same cadence (or slower) and looks for any audit scope where a recorded attestation disagrees with the live chain. Each divergence becomes: 1. A `civicos.escalations` row at severity 'major', source 'substrate', reason 'witness-divergence:<scope>'. 2. A `civicos.federation_events` entry on channel 'constitutional', type 'audit.divergence', so any subscribed watcher sees it. Auth: CIVICOS_CRON_SECRET as Authorization: Bearer (header only). Cadence: every 15 minutes (same as witness-sweep, but staggered). Idempotent: re-recording the same divergence is silently deduplicated by escalation reason — the operator sees one row, not one per cron tick. Only signed rows count (go-live review H-1): attestations recorded with a registered witness key (public.civicos_signed_witnesses), whose signature over `scope|seq|hash|label` verifies here against that key, and whose key had not been revoked when the row was recorded. Anything else (older unsigned rows, a row whose signature does not verify) never raises an alarm; rows that fail verification are counted as `unverified`.

get.description: Witness-sweep cron — emits a substrate-self attestation per visible scope. The substrate becomes its own first witness, so even before any external auditor signs the chain there's a continuous attestation timeline. Any divergence between the cron's recorded hash and the live hash is a tamper indicator. Auth: CIVICOS_CRON_SECRET as Authorization: Bearer (header only). Cadence: recommended every 15 minutes. Idempotent per (scope, seq): attestations are insert-only, so a point already attested is reported as such and never replaced. Signed (go-live review H-1): the platform signs `scope|seq|hash|label` with its audit signing key (Ed25519, lib/keys/custody.ts) and registers that public key for the self-witness label before its first attestation of the run (idempotent), so the divergence watchdog can verify these rows like any other witness's.

post.description: /api/federation/webhooks/test — send a synthetic signed ping to one registered federation webhook, so an operator can confirm an endpoint is reachable and validates the HMAC signature BEFORE relying on it for real events. The ping is out-of-band: it does NOT advance the delivery cursor and a failure does NOT count toward the circuit breaker. Go-live review M-5: the ping goes through the platform's safe fetch (lib/events/substrate-webhook.ts: public addresses only unless CIVICOS_WEBHOOKS_PRIVATE=1, no redirects), and the answer is coarse — delivered or not, never the remote status or error text, so the route cannot be used to probe addresses. The reason is logged for operators. Auth: a platform administrator's substrate session (platform-admin) OR CIVICOS_PROVISIONING_SECRET as a bearer (go-live review M-7); officials through the API are administrators only (lib/auth/roles.ts ADMIN_ONLY /api/federation). The secret lives only in the service-role-readable table, so the signing happens server-side here — the browser never sees it.

get.description: /api/health — diagnostic ping with a substrate reachability probe. Public (no auth) — returns minimal information so it's safe to expose to monitoring systems. Reports: ok flag, substrate-configured flag, substrate-reachable flag (via a cheap count on a public view), and where the platform keeps its state (lib/data/persist.ts): mode, last save, this server's role as state writer, who holds the writer's lease, and any error. Probes (Helm chart): `?live` answers at once without asking the substrate (liveness); `?ready` answers 503 while this server cannot take changes (a standby without the writer's lease, a writer that stopped saving, or a failed restore), so no traffic reaches it (readiness). Without either, the answer is always 200, as before. Also: what the installation is (production, training or demo, lib/ops/mode.ts). And (counts only, nothing personal): the platform audit chain (entries, intact), twin sources overdue against their schedule, warnings and errors logged in the last hour, whether traces go to the nation's collector, and an overall status: ok, degraded (something needs attention but changes are safe) or down (changes are not safe). With CIVICOS_STATE=postgres, `persistence.database` reports the per-record tables (lib/data/repo/postgres.ts): the adapter, PostGIS, the write queue's depth, how far behind other instances' changes this one is (outbox lag) and any write error, and the per-record documents every other store is kept as (stores, records, merges). A standby there still serves reads and record changes (every change, once every store is in the tables: a follower), so it reports ready while its tables are healthy.

post.description: /api/health — diagnostic ping with a substrate reachability probe. Public (no auth) — returns minimal information so it's safe to expose to monitoring systems. Probes (Helm chart): `?live` answers at once without asking the substrate (liveness); `?ready` answers 503 while this server cannot take changes (a standby without the writer's lease, a writer that stopped saving, or a failed restore), so no traffic reaches it (readiness). Without either, the answer is always 200, as before. Also: what the installation is (production, training or demo, lib/ops/mode.ts). And (counts only, nothing personal): the platform audit chain (entries, intact), twin sources overdue against their schedule, warnings and errors logged in the last hour, whether traces go to the nation's collector, and an overall status: ok, degraded (something needs attention but changes are safe) or down (changes are not safe). With CIVICOS_STATE=postgres, `persistence.database` reports the per-record tables (lib/data/repo/postgres.ts): the adapter, PostGIS, the write queue's depth, how far behind other instances' changes this one is (outbox lag) and any write error, and the per-record documents every other store is kept as (stores, records, merges). get.description: Substrate digest API — programmatic equivalent of the /gov/substrate "download digest" button. Computes per-view row counts and (optionally) the chain integrity sweep, returning a JSON snapshot. Auth: requires the CIVICOS_EXPORT_SECRET (Authorization: Bearer only, never ?token=). The endpoint uses the service-role client so counts are global (RLS-unfiltered) — that's what an external archive/auditor wants. Do not expose without the secret.

get.description: Comprehensive substrate export — compliance / handover artifact. Returns a single self-describing JSON document containing every row the configured service-role client can see across the lifecycle tables. The audit chain is included verbatim so the receiving party can re-verify integrity offline. Witnesses are included so a successor administration inherits the same tamper-after-the-fact proofs. Auth: CIVICOS_EXPORT_SECRET as Authorization: Bearer (never ?token=; lib/platform-auth.ts). Cost: O(rows). Capped per table via the ?cap query parameter (default 5000, max 50000) so a single response can't blow the lambda budget. Use the existing /api/substrate/digest endpoint for lightweight count snapshots; this endpoint is the full dump. Every dump is recorded (baseline audit §3.3): an audit-chain entry and an access-log entry (action `export`), naming the caller as the shared export secret (it names no person) with table and row counts only, never a row. The shared secret is to be replaced by named officials or two-official approval (integration register 1.46).

get.description: One twin entity: its stable id, the ids other systems use for it, its latest observations and the sources behind them. With Accept: application/ld+json the same entity as NGSI-LD (lib/twin/ngsi.ts): places as AdministrativeArea, facilities as PointOfInterest, observations as properties with observedAt; ?options=temporalValues gives every value over time. The JSON answer is unchanged.

post.description: Link a source system's own id to a twin entity (the crosswalk), so its rows resolve to the right place or institution. A named official; audited.

get.description: One subdivision as a GeoJSON feature with its observed values (?datetime), or one published site of the national facility register, or one unit of the published boundaries in force, or one published land parcel (public fields only). ?crs=<URI> serves it in another of the collection's coordinate systems (Part 2); Content-Crs names the one used.

OGC API – Features items: the nation's subdivisions as GeoJSON with their observed values (?limit, ?offset, ?bbox=minLon,minLat,maxLon,maxLat, ?datetime, ?level=1|2), or the national facility register's published sites (also ?category), as the viewer may see them, or the published boundaries in force (also ?level), or the land parcel register's published parcels (public fields only). Each collection's queryables (/collections/{id}/queryables) are accepted as equality filters (e.g. ?regionCode=KE-30&status=operational); any other parameter is refused with 400. CQL2 filters (OGC API – Features Part 3): ?filter=<CQL2-Text or CQL2-JSON>&filter-lang=cql2-text|cql2-json&filter-crs=CRS84 on the queryables and geometry (lib/twin/cql2.ts); an invalid filter is 400 with the reason. Coordinate systems (Part 2, lib/twin/ogc-crs.ts): ?crs=<URI> serves the features in EPSG:4326, EPSG:3857 or one of the nation's national grids (each collection lists them in `crs`), ?bbox-crs=<URI> reads bbox in one of them; the answer's Content-Crs header names the system of its coordinates.

OGC API – Features Part 3 queryables of one collection of the national twin: a JSON Schema of the properties a client may filter on, each accepted as a query parameter on /items (lib/twin/ogc-queryables.ts).
One OGC API – Features collection of the national twin, with the coordinate systems it serves (`crs`, `storageCrs`: OGC API – Features Part 2).

OGC API – Features collections of the national twin: the official subdivisions, the national facility register, the published boundaries and the land parcel register (public fields only), each with the coordinate systems it serves (Part 2: `crs`, `storageCrs`), and the systems offered across them (`crs`).
OGC API – Features conformance classes the twin's endpoint implements.
OGC API – Features landing page for the national twin (lib/twin/ogc.ts).

GET reads it; POST { fourEyesWithdrawal?: boolean, privateBrokers?: boolean } changes it, administrators only (ADMIN_ONLY in lib/auth/roles.ts), named and audited. post.description: Withdraw a twin import (a correction, lib/twin/register.ts): its observations are marked superseded from now, never deleted, so as-of queries for what was known before still see them. Each step is named and audited. A signed-in official's verified name replaces any name in the request (withOfficial), so the second official cannot be typed in.

Twin entities, sources and observations, substrate telemetry streams when the substrate is reachable, and the streams that receive pushed readings; restricted sites' positions as the viewer may see them (lib/twin/sta.ts). POST creates Observations on a twin stream source's Datastream (/Observations, /Datastreams('telemetry:<stream id>')/Observations, and the Data Array /CreateObservations), only with the key of the integration bound to that source (Authorization: Bearer civ_…, scope sta:write; BEARER_ROUTES in lib/auth/roles.ts). DELETE Observations('telemetry:<stream id>~<reading id>') with the same key withdraws a reading it sent (with ?reason=, a JSON { reason } or X-Reason): kept on record, no longer served or counted; a day already recorded has its run's withdrawal proposed to an official. PATCH and PUT answer 405 (update- entity is not offered: a correction is a new reading). See the service root's serverSettings for the conformance classes and what each covers. get.description: OGC SensorThings API v1.1 service root of the national twin (read-only): the entity sets (Things, Locations, Sensors, ObservedProperties, Datastreams, Observations) and the conformance classes served (lib/twin/sta.ts).

What the twin knew at a moment (?asOf=ISO time, default now): the latest value of each entity's metric recorded by then and true by then, with its source and run (lineage). ?knownAt= separates the two: true by asOf, as recorded by knownAt (e.g. knownAt=now for "true then, as known today"). Filter with ?metric= and ?entity=. A derived metric (lib/twin/derived.ts, e.g. population.share_65_plus) is computed from its inputs' observed values and answered as modelled, never observed: each value carries kind "modelled", the formula and the inputs it used (lib/twin/derived-server.ts); `derived` describes the formula.

post.description: Retire a tasking capability (lib/twin/tasking.ts retireCapability): POST { reason }. No new tasks for it; those already made run their course; the record stays. Administrators only (ADMIN_ONLY in lib/auth/roles.ts); the signed-in official's verified name is recorded (withOfficial); audited.

get.description: Tasking capabilities of the twin's stream sources (SensorThings Tasking Core, lib/twin/tasking.ts): GET lists them (retired ones included, marked); POST declares one: { sourceId, name, description?, actuator?: { name, description }, integrationId, parameters: [{ name, label, kind: number | text | choice | boolean, unit?, min?, max?, choices?, required? }] }. Administrators only (ADMIN_ONLY in lib/auth/roles.ts); a signed-in official's verified name replaces any name in the request (withOfficial); the executing integration must be approved and hold the scope sta:task; audited.

post.description: Tasking capabilities of the twin's stream sources (SensorThings Tasking Core, lib/twin/tasking.ts): GET lists them (retired ones included, marked); POST declares one: { sourceId, name, description?, actuator?: { name, description }, integrationId, parameters: [{ name, label, kind: number | text | choice | boolean, unit?, min?, max?, choices?, required? }] }. Administrators only (ADMIN_ONLY in lib/auth/roles.ts); a signed-in official's verified name replaces any name in the request (withOfficial); the executing integration must be approved and hold the scope sta:task; audited.

get.description: The national facility register as one PMTiles v3 archive (vector layer "facilities", zoom 0–12 by default), read with HTTP range requests (Range: bytes=a-b → 206 Partial Content; HEAD for the size and ETag). Open without sign-in: it holds only what the public may see — restricted sites at their generalised position, exactly as viewFacility() gives a viewer who is not signed in; confidential sites never. Rebuilt after publication changes (lib/twin/tiles-archive.ts) and kept as a file in the platform's data directory: a range request reads only the bytes it asks for from the file (in memory only where there is no writable directory). A new build has a new ETag, so a reader can tell its ranges came from one build (If-Range is honoured). Signed-in officials read the viewer-aware tiles at /api/twin/tiles/facilities/{z}/{x}/{y}.mvt, and an institution's own archive at /api/org/ministries/{id}/facilities/tiles.pmtiles.

One Mapbox Vector Tile (MVT 2.1) of the national facility register: layer "facilities", published sites as points with their id, national id, name, category, status, region and certification. Restricted sites are placed where the viewer may see them (generalised for viewers without need), so a tile is private to its viewer. y may end in .mvt or .pbf (lib/twin/tiles.ts).

One Mapbox Vector Tile (MVT 2.1) of the land parcel register: layer "parcels", published parcels as polygons with their public fields only (parcel id, land use, computed area, region and district, survey method and accuracy; never rights or holders), from zoom 13 (empty below it), simplified per zoom on a shared-edge topology (lib/twin/parcel-tiles.ts). The ETag changes with every published change; If-None-Match gives 304 until then. Zoom 0–20; y may end in .mvt or .pbf. Behind the official's session, or a GIS client's integration key or access token of scope ogc:read.

TileJSON 3.0.0 for the land parcel vector tiles: the tile address template (/api/twin/tiles/parcels/{z}/{x}/{y}.mvt), zoom range (from 13), bounds of the published parcels, the register's generation and the layer's fields (public only; lib/twin/parcel-tiles.ts).

get.description: What is waiting on officials across the government, from the records that hold it: every institution's queue (open or escalated items), its active incidents, permits awaiting a decision and open operational incidents. Read-only; the actions stay on their own endpoints (queue act, incident escalate/resolve, permit decide, ops incident ack/resolve), each audited. Cases and permits carry personal data: a signed-in official sees only those they may read (lib/auth/roles.ts canReadInstitution(), canReadPermits(); review M-3); the whole government and auditors see all of them. Open cases under approved procedures (lib/casework/) are listed without personal fields, only those the case rules let the official read (caseReadRefusal()), with the next deadline and whether a second official's approval is waiting.

Within what lib/auth/roles.ts lets the official read: counts, titles and configuration, never another institution's restricted records. "My work" is GET /api/work. GET only.

SuspensionPolicy.description: The suspension policy: platform safety defaults until the country adopts its own periods (who may suspend is the administrators until a country rule says otherwise; the platform does not invent emergency powers).

suspendBy.description: Who may suspend: any administrator (the default), or only the government-wide administrators (not an institution's own).

basis.description: Periods adopted before citations were required: the instrument as typed.

pending.description: A proposal waiting for its second official.

history.description: Adopted versions, oldest first; lapsed and withdrawn proposals are kept too.

delta.description: A delta from the previous release, when the mirror already holds it.

name.description: The key in a task's parameters, e.g. "samplingInterval".

sourceId.description: The stream source whose device it tasks.

integrationId.description: The integration that executes it (pulls and acknowledges its tasks).

period.description: The period it covers: YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-Qn.

link.description: The release or fallback incident the ticket is about.

tier.description: Contract tier at the time the ticket was opened: its targets apply.

waitingSince.description: The resolution clock pauses while the publisher waits on the nation.

why.description: What the track is for, in one plain sentence.

blockedBy.description: What outside the platform stops it (the environment, another track).

samplesOnly.description: Only in demo and training installations.

samplesCounted.description: Its checks read records that demo and training installations seed with samples, so "done" may rest on them.

TransitionRulesValues.description: The country's own rules for transitions (a rule set changed through policy-change.ts; none ships).

caretakerProcedures.description: Caretaker restrictions the nation's law or convention supports: procedure keys (or families, `procurement`) whose decisions are refused …

caretakerDecisions.description: … decision keys (`appoint`, `award`) refused under any procedure …

caretakerDirectives.description: … and kinds of directive (`policy`, `budget`) a caretaker issuer may not sign.

impeachmentStages.description: The institution that records each of the seven impeachment stages ('' where the nation has named none).

emergencyMaxDays.description: The longest an emergency declaration may run before it must be renewed (days); 0 while the nation has set none.

emergencyDeclarers.description: The institutions that may declare an emergency (`executive-office` for the whole government); empty: not named.

TransitionTerms.description: What a version of a transition says. A type alias so withDefaults() and policy-change take it as a plain record.

status.description: recorded: in force between its dates; ended: ended early (revoked, lifted), with a reason.

effectiveTo.description: Last day it applies (inclusive): an acting appointment's or delegation's end, an emergency's expiry.

institution.description: The institution concerned: the caretaker government (or `executive-office`), the dissolved body, a competence's previous holder.

actingInstitution.description: The institution that acts: dissolves, determines a succession, declares an emergency, the court, a competence's new holder.

powers.description: Delegated powers; an emergency's exceptional powers (as the declaration words them; never a platform permission).

regions.description: Regions from the nation's list; empty means the whole territory.

competence.description: A competence: the power or service affected (a register, a procedure family, a service).

target.description: Judicial review: the provision ruled on (eId absent: the whole instrument) and decisions ruled on directly.

reference.description: The court's case reference; a dissolution's or succession's instrument; a conflict's reference.

cases.description: Conflict of interest: the case ids or references the declarant steps aside from, and the interest declared.

stage.description: Impeachment: the stage this version records, and its outcome.

renews.description: Emergency: the declaration it renews, the trigger the law recognises, the permit types whose authority mapping is suspended under it.

arrangements.description: Transfers of records, assets, staff; election deadline after a dissolution; oversight and reporting; reasons.

next.description: Impeachment: the next stage open, and who records it.

code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 for the nation, ISO 3166-2 for subdivisions.

region.description: For places: the nation's operational region (setup) this is.

order.description: Its position in the nation's list of regions (official order).

uri.description: Its persistent identifier: https://<nation domain>/id/<kind>/<code>, resolved by /id/<kind>/<code> (entityUri).

fourEyesWithdrawal.description: Withdrawing an import needs a second official to confirm the proposal (default on).

privateBrokers.description: A stream's MQTT broker may resolve to a private or internal address (the nation's own network); default off.

withdrawn.description: Set when an official withdrew the import: its observations are superseded from that moment, never deleted. Under four-eyes, `by` confirmed what `proposedBy` proposed.

withdrawalProposed.description: A withdrawal proposed and waiting for a different official to confirm it (the nation's twin policy, lib/twin/policy.ts).

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the file as read (UTF-8 text), for provenance; absent on runs recorded before it was kept or that failed before reading. For a stream, of the samples read.

publisher.description: Who publishes it, e.g. "National Statistics Office".

kind.description: A CSV at an address or uploaded, or a substrate telemetry stream read as daily aggregates (lib/twin/stream.ts).

system.description: System name used in the crosswalk for this source's own entity ids.

format.description: The file's format: plain CSV with the mapping above (default), or SDMX-CSV 1.0/2.0, SDMX-JSON 2.0/1.0 or SDMX-ML 2.1 structure-specific data, read by lib/twin/sdmx.ts.

licence.description: The licence the publisher releases the data under (for the catalogue), when stated.

institution.description: The official's institution, when they serve one.

UnauthenticatedCount.description: Calls without a recognised key (or refused by a rate limit), counted per channel, ministry and result.

feedId.description: The feed or client whose own limit refused the call, when it was known.

upgradePath.description: Release ids, in order, that take the installed version to the latest.

advisories.description: Halted or withdrawn releases this nation runs: falling back is advised.

UsagePolicy.description: What a partner may do with data received under a grant (ODRL-like; lib/exchange/usage-policy.ts).

purposes.description: Purposes the data may be used for (short words, e.g. "oversight", "statistics").

retentionDays.description: Days the partner may keep the data.

onwardSharing.description: Whether the partner may pass the data on to a third party.

configured.description: Configured lists the platform keeps elsewhere (by the specification's name).

Verification.description: The result of checking one answer with an exchange service (lib/exchange/services.ts).

note.description: Why it was not performed, in words (no provision of law in force allows it, the service did not answer).

status.description: A certificate of the platform's register (lib/records/certificates.ts): its standing and whether its seal verifies.

sample.description: Sample credentials (VC-…, REV-…) exist only in demonstration and training installations.

persons.description: The people it concerns: the child or the deceased, the spouses.

parents.description: Parents of a birth, informant of any event.

form.description: Marriages: the form the law recognises (civil, customary, religious…).

sample.description: Registered from a sample case in a demo or training run (lib/casework/engine.ts `sampleMark`); absent on real records.

names.description: Whether members' names are recorded with a vote: always, only on a division, or never.

quorum.description: Members who must take part (yes, no or abstain) for a vote to count.

membership.description: Seats in the chamber (needed for majorities of all members).

locale.description: The nation's language and whether the notes are in it.

pending.description: True when the nation's language is not English and no translation exists yet.

WorkCase.description: An open case under an approved procedure (lib/casework/), without personal fields.

placeHistory.description: Earlier places, oldest first (a place is moved or cleared, never overwritten silently).

receivedAt.description: When the case reached the institution; its age is counted from this. Absent on examples.

source.description: Where the case came from: an example of the platform, a loaded file, typed in, or a connected case system. Absent means example.

feedId.description: The connected case system (CaseFeed) that sent it; only that system updates it.

importId.description: The load (lib/data/case-import.ts) a case came in with.

actedAt.description: When an official last assigned, escalated or closed it.

anonymisedAt.description: Set when the nation's retention rule removed its details (lib/data/retention.ts).

delegations.description: Delegations are not yet recorded on this installation (plan phase 6).
